 Government of Chhattisgarh 
 Chhattisgarh Raises DA for IAS, IPS and Other All India Services Officers to 63%; 3% Hike Effective from July 1 
 The Chhattisgarh government has increased the Dearness Allowance (DA) for Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS) and other All India Services officers serving in the state from 60% to 63%.
 The 3-percentage-point increase will be effective retrospectively from July 1, 2026. The revised DA will be paid in cash, along with the arrears due from the effective date. The General Administration Department (GAD) has issued an order approving the revised DA rates for members of the All India Services posted in Chhattisgarh.
 Revised DA Follows Centre’s October 29 Decision 
 The state government’s decision follows a memorandum issued by the Department of Expenditure under the Union Ministry of Finance on October 29, 2026.Through the memorandum, the Central Government approved a 3-percentage-point increase in DA for its employees, raising the rate from 60% to 63%, with effect from July 1, 2026.
 The Chhattisgarh government has extended the revised rates to All India Services officers serving in the state under Rule 3 of the All India Services (Dearness Allowance) Rules, 1972.
 How Will the Revised DA Be Calculated? 
 According to the government order, Dearness Allowance will be calculated on the basis of the pay drawn at the respective level in the pay matrix.However, special pay and personal pay will not be included while calculating the revised DA.
 The order also clarifies that the Dearness Allowance will not be treated as pay under Fundamental Rule 9(21).Any excess payment made contrary to the provisions of the order will be recoverable from the concerned officer.
 How Will Officers Receive DA Arrears? 
 The government has laid down the procedure for processing arrears arising from the retrospective revision.The bills for arrears will be prepared by the respective salary-disbursing offices from which the officers drew their salaries during the relevant period.
 The order further clarifies that individual authorisation letters will not be issued separately to officers. Instead, their salary slips will be treated as revised in accordance with the government order. The revised DA will be paid after adjusting any amounts already disbursed.
 With the latest decision, IAS, IPS and other All India Services officers serving in Chhattisgarh will receive DA at the revised rate of 63%, with the financial benefit applicable from July 1, 2026.
